chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'What is your view if I were to find a louse or a bug upon me, can I throw them off?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, and their young ones. They tend to ascend in other than their place of ascending'.
ai.seo_question: Can a person in Ihram kill or remove lice and bugs from their body?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that lice (*qurad*) and their young (*sighar*) may be removed by a person in Ihram, distinguishing them from the general prohibition on killing flying insects. The Imam explains that while they are insects, their mode of movement and existence ('ascension') differs from the typical flying insects whose killing is strictly forbidden, thereby providing a nuanced legal exception for these specific pests.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘What is your<sup>asws</sup> view if I were to find mite upon me, or a bug, can I throw these off?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, and their young ones. They tend to ascend in other than their place of ascending’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Najran from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who in the state of Ihram finds ticks and bigger ticks; can he throw it away? He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, he can do so. It is very mean of them to climb where they are not to climb.’”
